timeline.caption: Five orbits around one star. Watch them come home together.

timeline.text:
Where it is draws an ellipse.
How fast it goes draws a circle.

timeline.caption: The blue arrow is the velocity: which way, and how fast.
Stamp it at twelve equal moments of the year.
Now slide every arrow so all the tails meet.
The tips sit on a perfect circle. Hamilton, 1846.
The orbit is an ellipse. The velocity runs around a circle.
The velocity circle, written out.
GM over h sets the size: the circle's radius.
The eccentricity e only slides the circle's center upward.
Five orbits, stretched differently, with the same long axis.
Each long axis has the same length, 2a. Only its position shifts.
The energy depends only on a, never on the shape.
Same a, same period: all five come home together.

timeline.text:
Every circle passes
through the same two points.

timeline.caption: Their velocity circles come in every size and height.
Yet all five pass through the same two gold points.
The circular orbit's circle has radius p0, fixed by the energy.
R: the radius of a velocity circle.
d: how far its center sits above the origin.
p0: the same for every orbit of this energy.

timeline.text: Lift the plane onto a sphere.

timeline.caption: A glass sphere of radius p0. Its equator is the p0 circle.
From the north pole, draw a line through each point.

params.path: each point moves along its projection ray

timeline.caption: Every circle lands as a great circle, hinged on the gold points.
Stereographic projection: circles stay circles.
Look straight down the hinge: every ring becomes a line.
Alpha, the ring's tilt, is the whole shape of the orbit.

timeline.target: alpha sweep of the e = 0.55 ring to 90 degrees
timeline.caption: Push e toward 1 and the ring stands up through the north pole.
A head-on fall reaches infinite speed. Here it is one point.

timeline.text:
Rotate the sphere,
change the orbit.

timeline.caption: Rotate a ring about the hinge: the orbit stretches, same energy.
Earth's ring tilts 0.96 degrees. Halley's comet's tilts 75.3.
Fock, 1935: the same sphere, in four dimensions, organizes hydrogen.

timeline.text: Every orbit is a great circle.

constraints: Manim CE 0.19+ (validated on 0.20.1), Cairo renderer, single self-contained file, one ThreeDScene subclass
Camera moves only via self.move_camera / self.set_camera_orientation and ambient rotation; never .animate on the camera
Formulas that get zoomed (hodograph, energy_period, hinge_identity, tilt_card) live in world space; captions, headlines, stereo_formula, hydrogen_formula, labels and the inset are fixed in frame

camera.should_apply_shading is False; all lighting is computed explicitly per frame from the camera eye position, which is derived from phi and theta with generate_rotation_matrix so it is never stale
Depth sorting: sphere faces and ring segments set shade_in_3d = True so the ThreeDCamera orders them by depth
Planet motion obeys Kepler's equation; the synchronized return after 2 pi of sim time is exact
At most one headline or two text blocks on screen; captions replace each other
No external assets, no file IO, no network, seeded randomness only
acceptance: In the cold open and in Act 2 all planets are at perihelion at t = 0 and again at t = 2 pi (frame check: all planet dots on the +x axis).
The twelve stamped arrows land with their tips on the e = 0.6 hodograph circle to within 0.01 world units.
Every formula on screen has a caption on screen at the same time.
Each of the five lifted rings passes through both gold hinge points, and in the hinge-axis view every ring is a straight line through the sphere's center.
The camera reaches zoom 3.0 exactly once, on alpha in the tilt card, and returns to zoom 1.0 afterward.
Ring segments behind the glass render dimmer than segments in front in every 3D frame.
Earth's ring is shown at 0.96 degrees and Halley's at 75.3 degrees, matching arcsin(e).
